newsitem.title: UK: Laura Ashley falls as H1 disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Laura Ashley falls as H1 disappoints.

text.p: Profit-taking pushed shares in clothes and furnishings retailer Laura Ashley lower on Tuesday after first half figures fell short of market expectations, traders said.
By 0840 GMT, the shares had slipped 15p to 200-1/2 on trading volume of 380,000.

Pre-tax profits rose to 5.2 million stg from 3.0 million stg the previous year while sales fell to 156.1 million from 164.6 million after a reduction in mail order and perfume activities and the sale of Australian operations last year. Underlying sales rose by 3.2 percent.
The group declared an interim dividend of 0.4 pence a share, the first interim payment since 1989.

"The figures were expected to be very good. They weren't that bad but weren't up to some of the forecasts. The European and U.S. side were disappointing though the UK results were very good," said one trader.
Clothing sales in the UK were up three percent, but fell four percent in the United States. Shop turnover in the UK was up 10 percent.
Europe performed poorly with home furnishings sales down 10 percent and clothing down six percent.
"The shares had a very good performance coming up to these results so if they didn't come out with absolutely sparkling figures they were bound to see some profit-taking," he said.
In the first seven weeks of the second half, like-for-like shop sales rose six percent.
Trading remained on track and the outlook for the second half remained unchanged, the company said.
